A_target.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] and $f \in K \sqbrk x$ non-constant.
Then there is a [[Definition:Field Extension|field extension]] $L \supseteq K$ in which $f$ has a [[Definition:Root of Polynomial|root]].

B_source.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]] and $M$ a [[Definition:Maximal Ideal of Ring|maximal ideal]].
Then $R / M$ is a field.

substitutions.the maximal ideal M: the ideal generated by an irreducible factor g of f

derived.the class of x: a root of f in the quotient field

object_map.reformulation: Collapse K[x] by an irreducible factor of f, so that the class of x becomes a root.

validity_conditions: K[x] is a principal ideal domain, so an irreducible element generates a maximal ideal.
A field homomorphism out of K is injective, so K embeds in the quotient.
proof_plan: As $K \sqbrk x$ is a [[Definition:Unique Factorization Domain|unique factorization domain]], $f$ has an irreducible factor $g$.

In the [[Definition:Principal Ideal Domain|principal ideal domain]] $K \sqbrk x$, $\ideal g$ is maximal.
By the source result, $L = K \sqbrk x / \ideal g$ is a field.
The composite $K \to K \sqbrk x \to L$ is a ring homomorphism out of a field, hence injective, so $L$ is an extension of $K$.

Let $\alpha$ be the class of $x$.
Then $\map g \alpha$ is the class of $g$, which is $0$, so $\map f \alpha = 0$.
This is [[Kronecker's Theorem]].
{{qed}}
